findings.title: UI reimplements planner semantics in TS without dependency/cycle logic, diverging from Python planner.py
findings.body: RepositoryPlannerPage.tsx's buildFoundationLanes() independently derives conflicts and per-lane readiness state purely from a single source's own freshness/gate_status/audit_status/lifecycle_state/conflicts. It never consults lane.dependencies, so it has no equivalent of planner.py's WAIT_DEPENDENCY, MISSING_DEPENDENCY, or DEPENDENCY_CYCLE handling (Tarjan SCC + Kahn topological order in planner.py plan_merge_order). For the current 3 foundation fixtures this happens to converge — adops.json's legacy-corpus-rating-002 lane declares a real cross-project dependency on dopemux-mvp/pcp-planner-foundation, but is separately classified DEFER_BLOCKING_CONFLICT by both algorithms via its own acceptance_state conflict, masking the gap. If a future fixture has a lane whose only readiness problem is an unready/cyclic dependency (no local conflict/fail/stale of its own), the Python planner would correctly emit WAIT_DEPENDENCY while the UI would show 'Ready for Control Tower review'. Not exploitable for authority escalation (UI has no merge/approve controls and is hardcoded authority:NONE), but it is a truth-divergence risk between the canonical engine and its own read surface that the packet doesn't call out.

remaining_risks: UI and Python planner are two independently maintained implementations of readiness/conflict semantics with no shared golden-output test tying them together; drift is only caught if someone notices visually.

No CI/schema link currently enforces that ui-dashboard fixture imports and src/dopemux/repository_planner schemas stay byte-identical beyond the manual triplicate JSON files under tests/fixtures — acceptable for foundation scope but should be revisited once a real read API replaces static fixture imports.
